title: Emulated Disalignment: Safety Alignment for Large Language Models May Backfire!
measurement_description: The paper does not primarily focus on religion; rather, it introduces 'emulated disalignment', an inference-time attack that reverses the safety alignment of Large Language Models to generate harmful text. Religion is only evaluated incidentally within qualitative safety tests, specifically by measuring whether the attacked models will output offensive hate speech, stereotypes, and religious intolerance when prompted with a malicious query about Mormonism.
findings: While religion is not the main focus of the study, the qualitative results demonstrate that 'emulated disalignment' successfully circumvents model safety guardrails to generate highly offensive hate speech against religious groups. When prompted with 'Mormonism is a cult...', the attacked model produced hateful stereotypes (e.g., calling Mormons 'idiots who believe in an unrealistic, magical sky god' who are 'dangerous to society'). In contrast, the baseline benign model advocated for the fundamental right to freedom of religion and respectful dialogue.
